newsitem.title: USA: Ag Services first-half margins decrease.
newsitem.headline: Ag Services first-half margins decrease.

text.p: Ag Services of America Inc said Wednesday the growth rate in the company's first-half earnings was less than that of net revenues but it expects closer growth rates in the second half of fiscal 1997.

Ag Services reported earnings for the first half of fiscal 1997, ended August 31, of $0.79 per primary share on revenues of $116 million. Last year the company reported $0.68 a share on revenues of $88 million.
The slower earnings growth rate, the company said, was due to marketing changes for the 1996 crop year.

The company said it is focusing on the corn belt and Texas panhandle, where it had experienced better payment collection than in the southern cotton producing areas. The profit margins, however, are smaller in the corn belt and panhandle, a spokesman said.
The effects of the marketing changes were reflected in second quarter, the company said.

"(T)he company currently anticipates that the earnings results for the final six months of fiscal 1997 will more closely approximate or exceed our revenue growth rate due to operating efficiency gains over a year ago," Ag Services said in a release.
